sanskrit: nānāvihagasaṃghuṣṭaṃ nānādaṃṣṭrisamākulam kiṃnarair apsarobhiś ca devair api ca sevitam
english: It resounded with many kinds of birds, and was filled with many fanged creatures; it was frequented by kinneras and apsarases and even by the gods.

sanskrit: ekādaśa sahasrāṇi yojanānāṃ samucchritam adho bhūmeḥ sahasreṣu tāvatsv eva pratiṣṭhitam
english: It rose eleven thousand yojanas above the earth, and was planted just as deep — by the same number of thousands — below the ground.

sanskrit: tam uddhartuṃ na śaktā vai sarve devagaṇās tadā viṣṇum āsīnam abhyetya brahmāṇaṃ cedam abruvan
english: All the hosts of gods were unable to uproot it; so they approached Viṣṇu where he sat, and together with Brahmā they spoke as follows.

sanskrit: bhavantāv atra kurutāṃ buddhiṃ naiḥśreyasīṃ parām mandaroddharaṇe yatnaḥ kriyatāṃ ca hitāya naḥ
english: "Let the two of you apply your highest wisdom to this matter; let effort be made to uproot Mandara for our benefit."

sanskrit: tatheti cābravīd viṣṇur brahmaṇā saha bhārgava tato 'nantaḥ samutthāya brahmaṇā paricoditaḥ nārāyaṇena cāpy uktas tasmin karmaṇi vīryavān
english: "So be it," said Viṣṇu together with Brahmā, O descendant of Bhṛgu. Then mighty Ananta, roused by Brahmā and urged also by Nārāyaṇa, arose to the task.

sanskrit: atha parvatarājānaṃ tam ananto mahābalaḥ ujjahāra balād brahman savanaṃ savanaukasam
english: Then great-armed Ananta, immensely powerful, forcibly uprooted that king of mountains, O Brahmin, together with its forests and all the creatures dwelling in them.

sanskrit: tatas tena surāḥ sārdhaṃ samudram upatasthire tam ūcur amṛtārthāya nirmathiṣyāmahe jalam
english: Then the gods, together with him, approached the ocean and said to it: "For the sake of the nectar of immortality, we shall churn your waters."

sanskrit: apāṃpatir athovāca mamāpy aṃśo bhavet tataḥ soḍhāsmi vipulaṃ mardaṃ mandarabhramaṇād iti
english: The lord of the waters then spoke: "Then let a share fall to me as well; for I shall endure the great churning pressure from the rotation of Mandara."

sanskrit: ūcuś ca kūrmarājānam akūpāraṃ surāsurāḥ girer adhiṣṭhānam asya bhavān bhavitum arhati
english: The gods and asuras also addressed Akūpāra, the king of tortoises: "You ought to serve as the support for this mountain."

sanskrit: kūrmeṇa tu tathety uktvā pṛṣṭham asya samarpitam tasya śailasya cāgraṃ vai yantreṇendro 'bhyapīḍayat
english: The tortoise agreed, saying "So be it," and offered his back as its foundation; and Indra pressed down the summit of that mountain with a device to hold it firm.

sanskrit: manthānaṃ mandaraṃ kṛtvā tathā netraṃ ca vāsukim devā mathitum ārabdhāḥ samudraṃ nidhim ambhasām amṛtārthinas tato brahman sahitā daityadānavāḥ
english: Making Mandara the churning-rod and Vāsuki the rope, the gods — together with the daityas and dānavas — then began, O Brahmin, to churn the ocean, that treasure-house of waters, all intent upon the nectar of immortality.

sanskrit: ekam antam upāśliṣṭā nāgarājño mahāsurāḥ vibudhāḥ sahitāḥ sarve yataḥ pucchaṃ tataḥ sthitāḥ
english: The great asuras clung to one end of the serpent-king, while all the gods together took their position at the tail end.

sanskrit: ananto bhagavān devo yato nārāyaṇas tataḥ śira udyamya nāgasya punaḥ punar avākṣipat
english: The divine Lord Ananta stood where Nārāyaṇa stood; he repeatedly lifted the head of the great serpent and hurled it down again.

sanskrit: vāsuker atha nāgasya sahasākṣipyataḥ suraiḥ sadhūmāḥ sārciṣo vātā niṣpetur asakṛn mukhāt
english: As the serpent Vāsuki was repeatedly pulled back and forth by the gods, smoke-laden winds with tongues of flame poured again and again from his mouth.

sanskrit: te dhūmasaṃghāḥ saṃbhūtā meghasaṃghāḥ savidyutaḥ abhyavarṣan suragaṇāñ śramasaṃtāpakarśitān
english: Those billowing masses of smoke became cloud-banks flashing with lightning, and they rained down upon the hosts of gods who were worn thin by exertion and scorching heat.

sanskrit: tasmāc ca girikūṭāgrāt pracyutāḥ puṣpavṛṣṭayaḥ surāsuragaṇān mālyaiḥ sarvataḥ samavākiran
english: And showers of flowers falling from the rocky peak scattered garlands over the hosts of gods and asuras on all sides.

sanskrit: babhūvātra mahāghoṣo mahāmegharavopamaḥ udadher mathyamānasya mandareṇa surāsuraiḥ
english: A tremendous roar arose there, like the sound of great thunder-clouds, as the ocean was churned with Mandara by the gods and asuras.

sanskrit: tatra nānājalacarā viniṣpiṣṭā mahādriṇā vilayaṃ samupājagmuḥ śataśo lavaṇāmbhasi
english: There, in the salt waters, hundreds of aquatic creatures of every kind, crushed by the great mountain, met their dissolution.

sanskrit: vāruṇāni ca bhūtāni vividhāni mahīdharaḥ pātālatalavāsīni vilayaṃ samupānayat
english: The mountain also brought about the destruction of various beings of Varuṇa's realm, of many kinds, dwelling in the depths of the underworld.

sanskrit: tasmiṃś ca bhrāmyamāṇe 'drau saṃghṛṣyantaḥ parasparam nyapatan patagopetāḥ parvatāgrān mahādrumāḥ
english: As the mountain spun around, great trees with birds perched on them crashed against one another and fell from the mountain's peaks.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ saṃgharṣajaś cāgnir arcirbhiḥ prajvalan muhuḥ vidyudbhir iva nīlābhram āvṛṇon mandaraṃ girim
english: Fire born from their friction blazed repeatedly with its tongues of flame and covered Mount Mandara, as lightning covers a dark cloud.

sanskrit: dadāha kuñjarāṃś caiva siṃhāṃś caiva viniḥsṛtān vigatāsūni sarvāṇi sattvāni vividhāni ca
english: It burned elephants and lions fleeing from it, and all manner of creatures of every kind lost their lives.

sanskrit: tam agnim amaraśreṣṭhaḥ pradahantaṃ tatas tataḥ vāriṇā meghajenendraḥ śamayām āsa sarvataḥ
english: Indra, the foremost of the immortals, then quenched that blazing fire on all sides with water drawn from rain-clouds.

sanskrit: tato nānāvidhās tatra susruvuḥ sāgarāmbhasi mahādrumāṇāṃ niryāsā bahavaś cauṣadhīrasāḥ
english: Then many kinds of sap flowed into the ocean's waters — resins from the great trees and the juices of many medicinal plants.

sanskrit: teṣām amṛtavīryāṇāṃ rasānāṃ payasaiva ca amaratvaṃ surā jagmuḥ kāñcanasya ca niḥsravāt
english: Through those life-giving juices, through the milk of the ocean, and through the flowing of gold, the gods attained immortality.

sanskrit: atha tasya samudrasya taj jātam udakaṃ payaḥ rasottamair vimiśraṃ ca tataḥ kṣīrād abhūd ghṛtam
english: Then the water of that ocean became like milk, mixed with the finest of juices; and from that milk ghee was produced.

sanskrit: tato brahmāṇam āsīnaṃ devā varadam abruvan śrāntāḥ sma subhṛśaṃ brahman nodbhavaty amṛtaṃ ca tat
english: Then the gods spoke to Brahmā, who sat as the boon-granter: "We are utterly exhausted, O Brahmin, and still the nectar has not appeared."

sanskrit: ṛte nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ daityā nāgottamās tathā cirārabdham idaṃ cāpi sāgarasyāpi manthanam
english: "Without the god Nārāyaṇa — the daityas, the great serpents, and we ourselves alike — and this churning of the ocean, long begun, has gone on without result."

sanskrit: tato nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ brahmā vacanam abravīt vidhatsvaiṣāṃ balaṃ viṣṇo bhavān atra parāyaṇam
english: Then Brahmā spoke a word to the divine Nārāyaṇa: "Bestow strength upon all these, O Viṣṇu; you are the refuge here."

sanskrit: viṣṇur uvāca balaṃ dadāmi sarveṣāṃ karmaitad ye samāsthitāḥ kṣobhyatāṃ kalaśaḥ sarvair mandaraḥ parivartyatām
english: Viṣṇu said: "I give strength to all who are engaged in this task. Let the vessel be agitated by all; let Mandara be made to revolve."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca nārāyaṇavacaḥ śrutvā balinas te mahodadheḥ tat payaḥ sahitā bhūyaś cakrire bhṛśam ākulam
english: The Sūta said: Hearing the words of Nārāyaṇa, those powerful ones together churned the milk of the great ocean once more, vigorously.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatasahasrāṃśuḥ samāna iva sāgarāt prasannabhāḥ samutpannaḥ somaḥ śītāṃśur ujjvalaḥ
english: Then the Moon, lord of a hundred thousand rays, arose from the ocean like a second sun — radiant and serene, with its cool beams blazing bright.

sanskrit: śrīr anantaram utpannā ghṛtāt pāṇḍuravāsinī surā devī samutpannā turagaḥ pāṇḍuras tathā
english: Next arose Śrī, clad in white garments, born from the ghee; then arose Surā, the goddess of wine; and likewise a white horse.

sanskrit: kaustubhaś ca maṇir divya utpanno 'mṛtasaṃbhavaḥ marīcivikacaḥ śrīmān nārāyaṇaürogataḥ
english: The divine Kaustubha gem arose as well, born of the amṛta, its rays blazing brilliantly; it was glorious, and came to rest upon the breast of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: śrīḥ surā caiva somaś ca turagaś ca manojavaḥ yato devās tato jagmur ādityapatham āśritāḥ
english: Śrī, Surā, Soma, and the horse swift as thought — all went where the gods went, taking the path of the sun.

sanskrit: dhanvantaris tato devo vapuṣmān udatiṣṭhata śvetaṃ kamaṇḍaluṃ bibhrad amṛtaṃ yatra tiṣṭhati
english: Then the god Dhanvantari, possessed of a beautiful form, arose, bearing the white kamaṇḍalu vessel in which the nectar of immortality resided.

sanskrit: etad atyadbhutaṃ dṛṣṭvā dānavānāṃ samutthitaḥ amṛtārthe mahān nādo mamedam iti jalpatām
english: On seeing this utterly wondrous thing, a great clamour arose among the dānavas, all crying out: "It is mine! It is mine!"

sanskrit: tato nārāyaṇo māyām āsthito mohinīṃ prabhuḥ strīrūpam adbhutaṃ kṛtvā dānavān abhisaṃśritaḥ
english: Then the Lord Nārāyaṇa assumed the enchanting illusion of Mohinī, taking on a wondrous female form, and approached the dānavas.

sanskrit: tatas tad amṛtaṃ tasyai dadus te mūḍhacetasaḥ striyai dānavadaiteyāḥ sarve tadgatamānasaḥ
english: Then all the dānavas and daityas, their minds deluded, their thoughts fixed entirely upon her, gave the nectar to that woman.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca athāvaraṇamukhyāni nānāpraharaṇāni ca pragṛhyābhyadravan devān sahitā daityadānavāḥ
english: The Sūta said: Then the daityas and dānavas, taking up various coverings and weapons of every kind, rushed together against the gods.

sanskrit: tatas tad amṛtaṃ devo viṣṇur ādāya vīryavān jahāra dānavendrebhyo nareṇa sahitaḥ prabhuḥ
english: Then the mighty god Viṣṇu, that powerful lord, together with Nara, took the nectar and carried it away from the lords of the dānavas.

sanskrit: tato devagaṇāḥ sarve papus tad amṛtaṃ tadā viṣṇoḥ sakāśāt saṃprāpya saṃbhrame tumule sati
english: Then all the hosts of gods, having received it from Viṣṇu, drank that nectar amid the tumultuous uproar and confusion.

sanskrit: tataḥ pibatsu tatkālaṃ deveṣv amṛtam īpsitam rāhur vibudharūpeṇa dānavaḥ prāpibat tadā
english: Then, at the very moment the gods were drinking the coveted nectar, the dānava Rāhu, having assumed the guise of a god, drank some of it.

sanskrit: tasya kaṇṭham anuprāpte dānavasyāmṛte tadā ākhyātaṃ candrasūryābhyāṃ surāṇāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: The moment the nectar reached the throat of that dānava, it was reported by the Moon and the Sun, who desired the welfare of the gods.

sanskrit: tato bhagavatā tasya śiraś chinnam alaṃkṛtam cakrāyudhena cakreṇa pibato 'mṛtam ojasā
english: Then the Blessed Lord, with his cakra-weapon, the adorned discus, swiftly severed the head of the dānava as he was drinking the nectar.

sanskrit: tac chailaśṛṅgapratimaṃ dānavasya śiro mahat cakreṇotkṛttam apatac cālayad vasudhātalam
english: That great head of the dānava, like a mountain peak, severed by the discus, fell to the earth and made it tremble.

sanskrit: tato vairavinirbandhaḥ kṛto rāhumukhena vai śāśvataś candrasūryābhyāṃ grasaty adyāpi caiva tau
english: From that time Rāhu, that disembodied head, formed an eternal enmity; to this very day he swallows the Moon and the Sun.

sanskrit: vihāya bhagavāṃś cāpi strīrūpam atulaṃ hariḥ nānāpraharaṇair bhīmair dānavān samakampayat
english: And the Blessed Lord Hari, abandoning that incomparable female form, shook the dānavas with many fearsome weapons.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravṛttaḥ saṃgrāmaḥ samīpe lavaṇāmbhasaḥ surāṇām asurāṇāṃ ca sarvaghorataro mahān
english: Then a great and utterly terrible battle broke out near the salt ocean between the gods and the asuras.

sanskrit: prāsāḥ suvipulās tīkṣṇā nyapatanta sahasraśaḥ tomarāś ca sutīkṣṇāgrāḥ śastrāṇi vividhāni ca
english: Long sharp javelins fell in thousands; spears with very sharp points, and weapons of every kind fell upon them.

sanskrit: tato 'surāś cakrabhinnā vamanto rudhiraṃ bahu asiśaktigadārugṇā nipetur dharaṇītale
english: Then asuras, cleaved by the discus, vomiting much blood, struck down by swords, spears, and maces, fell to the ground.

sanskrit: chinnāni paṭṭiśaiś cāpi śirāṃsi yudhi dāruṇe taptakāñcanajālāni nipetur aniśaṃ tadā
english: And in that terrible battle, heads severed by broad-bladed weapons, covered in nets of heated gold, fell again and again.

sanskrit: rudhireṇāvaliptāṅgā nihatāś ca mahāsurāḥ adrīṇām iva kūṭāni dhāturaktāni śerate
english: Great asuras, their limbs smeared with blood, slain, lay like the red-ore peaks of mountains.

sanskrit: hāhākāraḥ samabhavat tatra tatra sahasraśaḥ anyonyaṃ chindatāṃ śastrair āditye lohitāyati
english: Cries of lamentation arose by the thousands in every direction as they cut each other down with weapons while the sun turned blood-red.

sanskrit: parighaiś cāyasaiḥ pītaiḥ saṃnikarṣe ca muṣṭibhiḥ nighnatāṃ samare 'nyonyaṃ śabdo divam ivāspṛśat
english: The noise of those striking one another in battle with iron clubs of tawny hue and with fists in close combat seemed to touch the sky.

sanskrit: chindhi bhindhi pradhāvadhvaṃ pātayābhisareti ca vyaśrūyanta mahāghorāḥ śabdās tatra samantataḥ
english: "Cut! Pierce! Rush forward! Strike down! Charge!" — such terrifyingly fierce cries were heard on all sides.

sanskrit: evaṃ sutumule yuddhe vartamāne bhayāvahe naranārāyaṇau devau samājagmatur āhavam
english: While this dreadful and tumultuous battle raged, the divine pair Nara and Nārāyaṇa entered the fray.

sanskrit: tatra divyaṃ dhanur dṛṣṭvā narasya bhagavān api cintayām āsa vai cakraṃ viṣṇur dānavasūdanam
english: There, beholding Nara's divine bow, the Blessed Lord Viṣṇu also recalled to mind his discus, the destroyer of dānavas.

sanskrit: tato 'mbarāc cintitamātram āgataṃ; mahāprabhaṃ cakram amitratāpanam vibhāvasos tulyam akuṇṭhamaṇḍalaṃ; sudarśanaṃ bhīmam ajayyam uttamam
english: Then, the instant it was thought of, it came from the sky — the supremely radiant discus, scorcher of enemies, equal in brilliance to the sun, with its unblunted rim, the Sudarśana, fearsome, unconquerable, supreme.

sanskrit: tad āgataṃ jvalitahutāśanaprabhaṃ; bhayaṃkaraṃ karikarabāhur acyutaḥ mumoca vai capalam udagravegavan; mahāprabhaṃ paranagarāvadāraṇam
english: When it arrived, blazing with the radiance of kindled fire and striking terror, the unfailing Acyuta, whose arms are like an elephant's trunk, released it — swift and fiercely fast, supremely brilliant, destroyer of enemy citadels.

sanskrit: tad antakajvalanasamānavarcasaṃ; punaḥ punar nyapatata vegavat tadā vidārayad ditidanujān sahasraśaḥ; kareritaṃ puruṣavareṇa saṃyuge
english: Equal in brilliance to the fire of death, it flew back and again swiftly as it was hurled, rending the sons of Diti and Danu by the thousands, driven by the hand of that supreme being in battle.

sanskrit: dahat kva cij jvalana ivāvalelihat; prasahya tān asuragaṇān nyakṛntata praveritaṃ viyati muhuḥ kṣitau tadā; papau raṇe rudhiram atho piśācavat
english: Burning in one place, it licked like a flame; it violently cut down those hosts of asuras; sent spinning again and again through the sky and the earth, it drank blood in battle like a piśāca demon.

sanskrit: athāsurā giribhir adīnacetaso; muhur muhuḥ suragaṇam ardayaṃs tadā mahābalā vigalitameghavarcasaḥ; sahasraśo gaganam abhiprapadya ha
english: Then the asuras, undaunted in spirit and immensely powerful, with radiance like dispersing clouds, seized mountains and tormented the host of gods again and again, rising by the thousands into the sky.

sanskrit: athāmbarād bhayajananāḥ prapedire; sapādapā bahuvidhamegharūpiṇaḥ mahādrayaḥ pravigalitāgrasānavaḥ; parasparaṃ drutam abhihatya sasvanāḥ
english: Then from the sky there fell terror-inspiring great mountains with their trees, taking the form of many kinds of clouds, their topmost peaks crumbling away; they crashed swiftly against one another and roared.

sanskrit: tato mahī pravicalitā sakānanā; mahādripātābhihatā samantataḥ parasparaṃ bhṛśam abhigarjatāṃ muhū; raṇājire bhṛśam abhisaṃpravartite
english: Then the earth with all its forests shook violently, struck on all sides by the fall of great mountains, as the two sides roared fiercely at each other again and again on that great and fiercely raging battlefield.

sanskrit: naras tato varakanakāgrabhūṣaṇair; maheṣubhir gaganapathaṃ samāvṛṇot vidārayan giriśikharāṇi patribhir; mahābhaye 'suragaṇavigrahe tadā
english: Then Nara, with his mighty arrows tipped with fine gold, covered the sky's path and split the mountain peaks with feathered shafts, during that great and terrible battle with the host of asuras.

sanskrit: tato mahīṃ lavaṇajalaṃ ca sāgaraṃ; mahāsurāḥ praviviśur arditāḥ suraiḥ viyadgataṃ jvalitahutāśanaprabhaṃ; sudarśanaṃ parikupitaḥ niśāmya ca
english: Then the great asuras, tormented by the gods and seeing the Sudarśana blazing with the radiance of kindled fire and enraged as it coursed through the sky, plunged into the earth and into the salt-water ocean.

sanskrit: tataḥ surair vijayam avāpya mandaraḥ; svam eva deśaṃ gamitaḥ supūjitaḥ vinādya khaṃ divam api caiva sarvaśas; tato gatāḥ saliladharā yathāgatam
english: Then, with victory won by the gods, Mandara, duly honoured, was returned to its own place; it resounded through the sky and the heavens on all sides; and thereafter the clouds went their way as before.

sanskrit: tato 'mṛtaṃ sunihitam eva cakrire; surāḥ parāṃ mudam abhigamya puṣkalām dadau ca taṃ nidhim amṛtasya rakṣituṃ; kirīṭine balabhid athāmaraiḥ saha
english: Then the gods, filled with supreme and complete joy, placed the nectar in safe keeping; and Indra, slayer of Bala, together with the immortals, gave over that treasure of nectar to the Crowned One to guard.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca etat te sarvam ākhyātam amṛtaṃ mathitaṃ yathā yatra so 'śvaḥ samutpannaḥ śrīmān atulavikramaḥ
english: The Sūta said: All this has been told to you — how the nectar was churned forth — and it is in this account that the glorious horse of incomparable power was born.

sanskrit: yaṃ niśāmya tadā kadrūr vinatām idam abravīt uccaiḥśravā nu kiṃvarṇo bhadre jānīhi māciram
english: On seeing that horse, Kadrū then said to Vinatā: "What colour is Uccaiḥśravas, dear friend? Tell me without delay."

sanskrit: vinatovāca śveta evāśvarājo 'yaṃ kiṃ vā tvaṃ manyase śubhe brūhi varṇaṃ tvam apy asya tato 'tra vipaṇāvahe
english: Vinatā said: "This king of horses is purely white. What do you think, O auspicious one? Tell me your view of his colour, and then let us make a wager on it."

sanskrit: kadrūr uvāca kṛṣṇavālam ahaṃ manye hayam enaṃ śucismite ehi sārdhaṃ mayā dīvya dāsībhāvāya bhāmini
english: Kadrū said: "I believe this horse has a black tail, O bright-toothed one. Come, let us wager together on servitude, O passionate one."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca evaṃ te samayaṃ kṛtvā dāsībhāvāya vai mithaḥ jagmatuḥ svagṛhān eva śvo drakṣyāva iti sma ha
english: The Sūta said: Having thus made a compact with each other for servitude, the two went to their own homes, saying: "We shall look tomorrow."

sanskrit: tataḥ putrasahasraṃ tu kadrūr jihmaṃ cikīrṣatī ājñāpayām āsa tadā vālā bhūtvāñjanaprabhāḥ
english: Then Kadrū, wishing to play a trick, commanded her thousand sons to become hairs as black as collyrium and cling to the horse's tail.

sanskrit: āviśadhvaṃ hayaṃ kṣipraṃ dāsī na syām ahaṃ yathā tad vākyaṃ nānvapadyanta tāñ śaśāpa bhujaṃgamān
english: "Enter the horse quickly so that I shall not become a slave." Those serpents did not comply with that command, and she cursed them.

sanskrit: sarpasatre vartamāne pāvako vaḥ pradhakṣyati janamejayasya rājarṣeḥ pāṇḍaveyasya dhīmataḥ
english: "When the serpent sacrifice is being performed, fire shall consume you — at the sacrifice of Janamejaya, that wise royal sage, descendant of the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: śāpam enaṃ tu śuśrāva svayam eva pitāmahaḥ atikrūraṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ kadrvā daivād atīva hi
english: The Grandfather himself heard this curse, so exceedingly cruel as it was pronounced by Kadrū — heard it truly as if by fate.

sanskrit: sārdhaṃ devagaṇaiḥ sarvair vācaṃ tām anvamodata bahutvaṃ prekṣya sarpāṇāṃ prajānāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: Together with all the hosts of gods, he approved that pronouncement, seeing the great multitude of serpents and desiring the welfare of all living beings.

sanskrit: tigmavīryaviṣā hy ete dandaśūkā mahābalāḥ teṣāṃ tīkṣṇaviṣatvād dhi prajānāṃ ca hitāya vai prādād viṣahaṇīṃ vidyāṃ kāśyapāya mahātmane
english: For these biting serpents are possessed of fierce and potent venom and are of great power; on account of their sharp-venom nature, and truly for the welfare of living beings, he bestowed the science of snake-charming upon the great-souled Kāśyapa.
